story.text: It is Saturday morning. You wake up late and reach for your phone. It is 7:40.
story.cap: Read the story as if it were happening to you.

story.text: Last night, tired, you tapped a link in a message from a courier called Swift Parcel and typed your card details. The page showed an error, so you went to sleep. This morning a second message arrives.

items.html: Your phone buzzes. CyberReport has an optional feature that checks messages on your phone and warns you when one looks like a scam. You switched it on when you set up the app.

files.cap: The CyberReport alert over the new message

This alert would help me notice scams earlier
I would switch this alert on

items.note: The first four items are asked about how you would feel in the story.

items.prompt: What would make an alert like this acceptable to you?

story.text: Nothing has been charged. You are not sure the message even matters. Your friend says to ignore it. A colleague says you should report it, just in case.

story.text: You decide to report, then hesitate. Who will see your details? Could your family or your employer find out? Will people think you were careless?

items.html: CyberReport lets you report in two ways.

files.cap: Home: sign in to report, or report anonymously

options.l: Sign in to report (my identity is recorded, I can save drafts and get updates)
Report anonymously (no account, a private Case ID and access code)

story.text: Halfway through, your phone rings. It is work. You save your draft and take the call. Later that day, CyberReport sends you reminders.

items.html: Because you signed in, CyberReport can remind you to finish. Here are three reminders it might send on different days.
